title: Uyelgi cemetery
fact_summary: A cemetery of the late Kushnarenkovo culture in the Trans-Ural region, used from about the end of the 8th century to the 11th.

place.label: Trans-Ural region (east of the Ural mountains)
place.note: Pin placed by Claude in the region the studies name ('Trans-Ural'). The cemetery's exact position has not been checked.

claims.text: Uyelgi is a cemetery of the late Kushnarenkovo culture in the Trans-Ural region, “used from the end of eighth century to the eleventh century”.
claims.certainty_reason: One tier B study summarising the excavators' work. The excavation report itself has not been opened.

claims.text: It can be divided into at least three chronological horizons.
A 2022 study lists “Uyelgi, Karanayevo”, Russia (Ural), as Late Kushnarenkovo and dates them to the 9th–11th centuries.
claims.certainty_reason: One tier B study; the row groups Uyelgi with a second site.

dating_methods.text: Radiocarbon dates and stable isotope data are reported in the supplementary information of the 2020 study (chapter 2), not yet opened here.
dating_methods.certainty_reason: Where the dates are is stated in the study.

contradictions.what_differs: When the cemetery started: the end of the 8th century (2020 study) or the 9th century (2022 study's table, where Uyelgi shares a row with Karanayevo). The difference may come from that grouping; it is shown rather than settled.

open_questions.text: What does the excavation report say about the graves and grave goods?

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
